acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Raptors family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as War Eagle, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Carry-Off Champion archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two earth construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Huge eagle with battered primaries, heavy golden beak, scarred talons, broad wing shoulders, and dark mantle.
Signature mechanic: Committed Carry: lowered talons grip once, follow one shadow-marked ascent lane, and return through one fixed landing route.
battlefieldDuty: Grip and lift one target a short distance while lesser Raptors attack the exposed group below.
constructionDimensions: Thin mineral guards reinforce talons, beak ridge, shoulder joints, and selected primary shafts while flexible feathers remain dominant.
Detached grit and small stones orbit only near loaded wing or talon structures and fall visibly during recovery.
counterplay: Break the grip before lift or attack the predictable landing route when the Eagle returns. Affinity signal: A pale mineral fault opens at the planted talon, shoulder, or loaded feather row after commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Heavy rock wings that erase flight anatomy
identityInvariants: Every form retains an avian body with two wings, two taloned legs, hooked beak, feathered tail, and species-appropriate head rather than humanoid arms or torso.
Tier escalation uses wingspan, feather structure, facial disc, talon mass, scars, and flight behavior rather than worn equipment.
Shadow shape, tail fan, primary-feather angle, talon extension, perch choice, and landing route keep aerial attacks readable.
telegraph: Its legs lower, primary feathers spread, and the ascent lane lengthens in its shadow.
